data.title:
A Milford tradition.
One scoop at a time.
data.excerpt: Good ice cream. Good company. Right here on Elm Street.

data.title: An Elm Street tradition.
data.excerpt: Before the cones and the cups, there were cows, milk routes, and a family with a business to build.

children.text: Hayward’s story begins with local dairy farming. Before the ice cream windows, Charles Hayward worked for Whiting Dairy and bought a farm on Elm Street. His three sons helped carry the family business forward.
From dairy farm to roadside favorite

The roadside stand became part of that story. An early Hayward Farms postcard identifies the Milford building as a place where ice cream was made for its network of stands. It also advertises a snack bar, a reminder that the business has taken different forms over the years.

In Milford High School’s 1948 yearbook, a Hayward Farms advertisement offered dairy products, ice cream and frozen foods. It is a small but tangible link between the business and the people who grew up here.

In 2022, Hayward’s Family Ice Cream joined the New Hampshire Ice Cream Trail. Interviewed that summer, Frank Robinson described the Milford shop’s homemade ice cream and the individual batches behind it.
Today, the tradition continues at 383 Elm Street. Come back for your usual, bring someone along, or make a new favorite part of the story.
